title: Investigating a delivery complaint
text: SIMULATED OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE — portfolio demonstration, not an Olist policy. When a review describes a delayed or missing delivery, verify the historical order timestamps and delivery status before drawing conclusions. Escalate a confirmed unresolved issue through an appropriate support channel. Customer text describes an individual experience and does not establish carrier responsibility or the prevalence of a problem.
action: Verify the order timeline and status before escalating an unresolved delivery complaint.

title: Handling a damaged-item complaint
text: SIMULATED OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE — portfolio demonstration, not an Olist policy. If a customer reports damaged or broken goods, inspect the item record and request appropriate evidence through a private support channel. Record the complaint and consult the seller's actual terms before recommending any replacement or refund. This example does not authorize a refund or establish Olist's operational practices.
action: Review the item record and gather private damage evidence before consulting the seller's actual resolution terms.

title: Checking wrong or missing items
text: SIMULATED OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE — portfolio demonstration, not an Olist policy. For a complaint about a wrong or missing item, compare the customer's account with the order's individual item records. A multi-item order should not be treated as a single product. Keep the original complaint and item identifiers traceable. Do not infer a systematic seller problem from retrieved examples alone.
action: Compare the complaint with individual order items and preserve its source identifiers.

title: Communicating with customers
text: SIMULATED OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE — portfolio demonstration, not an Olist policy. Acknowledge the reported issue in the customer's preferred language. Distinguish verified order facts from unresolved allegations. Do not promise an arrival date, refund, or compensation that cannot be supported by authorized operational information. Keep personal information out of public replies.
action: Acknowledge the issue in the customer's language and communicate only verified facts without unsupported promises.

title: Interpreting historical evidence
text: SIMULATED OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE — portfolio demonstration, not an Olist policy. Treat Olist records as historical evidence. Use verified SQL for numerical cohort results and saved held-out predictions for model estimates. Retrieved reviews are qualitative examples, not a representative complaint survey. Experimental model probabilities are not delivery guarantees and do not establish causal drivers.
action: Use calculated cohort metrics for quantitative claims and retrieved reviews only as cited qualitative examples.
